subject: RedisWorks POC traffic onboarding — intake & next steps
messages:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan@redisworks.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@redisworks.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: RedisWorks trial scope and traffic details

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Priya and I talked through the proposed 30-day POC and want to confirm a few items so your team can size capacity and we can lock the kickoff. High level: we care most about latency under load for our chat endpoint and preserving answer fidelity compared to our current hosted model.

Quick answers from our side (see attached sample traffic in a moment):
- Primary workload: customer support chat (multi-turn). Typical user message tokens: 8–40; system prompts add ~50 tokens. Generated response tokens: 40–220 (median ~95).
- Concurrency target: 120 concurrent active sessions during business hours (US-EAST), with occasional multi-minute bursts up to 900 concurrent sessions for incident escalation windows lasting ~6–12 minutes.
- Steady-state RPS: 35 RPS average across the service, with expected 4x burst factor.
- Sensitive data: we will redact PII before sending, but we need assurance about log retention and KV cache isolation.

What we need from Redwood to proceed:
1) A proposed success matrix (latency P50/P95 targets, token cost budget, quality gates).
2) Recommended model variant/quantization profile for this workload and any fallback policy.
3) A 2-week timeline for environment prep + a 30-day trial window, with clear owners.

Priya will attach a small sample of traffic (anonymized) so you can validate header sizes and token distribution. We can be flexible on start date next week if you confirm capacity.

Thanks —
Ethan
Ethan Ross
Head of Platform, RedisWorks
ops@redisworks.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan@redisworks.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@redisworks.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RedisWorks trial scope and traffic details

Ethan — appreciate the clear summary and the token breakdown. That helps a lot. I pulled together a concise intake and next-step plan below so we have alignment before we ingest sample traffic.

POC goal (proposed): validate that Redwood can meet latency SLOs at RedisWorks' burst profile while staying within a target per-conversation token cost.

Proposed success matrix (draft):
- Latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms for generation-only path at 95% of steady-state; during burst windows, P95 < 700ms with graceful degradation (fallback to lower-capacity model variant).
- Quality: automated sampling comparing Rouge/EM-like metrics on a curated eval set (we'll share prompts) + manual QA pass on 50 end-to-end examples — pass rate >= 90%.
- Cost: token spend during trial not to exceed "X" (we'll translate to committed spend after sample traffic).

Initial owners and timeline:
- Redwood PM (me) — overall POC coordination and weekly readouts.
- Redwood Infra (Dev Patel) — bench provisioning, model variant selection, quant profile.
- RedisWorks (Ethan/Priya) — share traffic samples, provide eval prompt set, schedule kickoff.

Next steps I propose (action items):
1) Priya shares anonymized sample traffic CSV (token lengths, timestamped events, concurrency markers) — target: today or tomorrow.
2) Dev to validate infra assumptions and respond with recommended instance class + batch sizing within 24–36 hours of sample receipt.
3) We schedule a 30-minute kickoff once infra sizing is done; aim for environment ready in 7–10 business days after sizing.

Attachment placeholders: please attach the sample CSV and our short POC success template once available.

CC'ing Laura for budget/credit sign-off.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0133

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RedisWorks trial scope and traffic details

Stephanie / Laura —

Quick technical take after the initial numbers:
- The token lengths and median response size mean we should target 2x of the steady-state concurrency in GPU-backed serving headroom to cover KV cache and batching. For 120 steady concurrent sessions that suggests capacity for ~240 concurrent inference slots.
- For bursts up to 900 concurrent sessions: we'll introduce a multi-tier routing policy: dedicated reserved pool for steady state + autoscale pool (burst) with fallback variant (8-bit quantized) if scaling lag occurs.
- Batch sizing: recommend dynamic batching with a 6–8ms micro-batch window to balance latency and throughput for this workload.
- Telemetry hooks: please confirm we can collect sampled traces (not full payloads) for P95 debugging. We'll also wire a prefix-cache policy for repeated system prompts to save tokens.

I'll prepare a sizing note with instance classes and expected token spend by tomorrow EOD once we receive the sample.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya@redisworks.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Ross <ethan@redisworks.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 12:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RedisWorks trial scope and traffic details

Hi Stephanie / Dev —

Thanks — attaching the anonymized sample traffic CSV (redisworks_sample_traffic.csv) and a short success-matrix workbook (poc-success-matrix.xlsx). Quick clarifications:
- The timestamps in the CSV cover a 48-hour slice with two distinct bursts (one scheduled incident drill, one organic).
- We redacted PII and replaced IDs with hashed values; conversation context windows are preserved.
- We are comfortable with sampled telemetry for debugging as long as traces do not include user text.

We'd like to target a kickoff window the week of Aug 23. Once you confirm sizing/instance recommendations we can lock the date.

Thanks,
Priya
Resp., Operations
RedisWorks
ops@redisworks.com
